title: Few Blacks in Argentina; Latin American history
summary: They discuss absorption of Blacks in Argentina, England and Latin America and Spanish conquest.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: You know, that's one thing you notice in Argentina. Very few Blacks. They had Blacks, but it was...

Oh, there's very few. As soon as I went there with Ellington, I said, 'There's very few soul brothers here.' But there were Blacks there. Now, I would believe they were either absorbed or destroyed. Now, in England, I think in the Sixteenth Century they had a record of 7,000 Blacks. Within that century they disappeared. They had been assimilated, you know. As Blacks, they weren't there any more. They intermarried and...
Well, yes. But they weren't there as an entity as it were.
Yeah, but I've heard that they still have... what it...not the Orinoco or the Amazon River... Somewhere in the jungle that they still have some escaped...
Well, that could be. But in Argentina you don't see many Black people.

Well, that's a phenomenon. Well, that's another thing. Bringing it back... So therefore, there's Central America, Honduras, all those have had slavery, you can imagine... Now, we're speaking about a holocaust; this puts us in another bag, you know.
And look at all the Indians that have been...
Well, Mr. Cortez and Pisarro took good care of that when they brought with them... You must remember, when the Bible was written, they didn't know anything about this side of the world.
